The probability density function of a continuous random variable, $X$, is defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3}{16}(a - x^2), & 0 \le x \le 2, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$

questions.corrige_markdown:
For a probability density function the total area under the curve is $1$: $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1$. Since $f(x) = 0$ outside $[0, 2]$,

$$\int_0^2 \frac{3}{16}(a - x^2)\,dx = 1.$$

$$\frac{3}{16}\left[a x - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \frac{3}{16}\left(2a - \frac{8}{3}\right) = 1$$

$$2a - \frac{8}{3} = \frac{16}{3} \;\Longrightarrow\; 2a = \frac{24}{3} = 8 \;\Longrightarrow\; a = 4. \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Check: with $a = 4$, $f(x) = \frac{3}{16}(4 - x^2) \ge 0$ on $[0, 2]$, so it is a valid density.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Show that the median, $m$, of $X$ satisfies the equation $m^3 - 12m + 8 = 0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median $m$ is the value such that $P(X \le m) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, i.e. $\displaystyle\int_0^m f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}$ (with $0 \le m \le 2$).

$$\int_0^m \frac{3}{16}(4 - x^2)\,dx = \frac{3}{16}\left[4x - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^m = \frac{3}{16}\left(4m - \frac{m^3}{3}\right) = \frac{12m - m^3}{16}$$

Setting this equal to $\frac{1}{2}$:

$$\frac{12m - m^3}{16} = \frac{1}{2} \;\Longrightarrow\; 12m - m^3 = 8 \;\Longrightarrow\; m^3 - 12m + 8 = 0. \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Remark: let $g(m) = m^3 - 12m + 8$; $g(0) = 8 > 0$ and $g(1) = -3 < 0$, so the root in $[0, 2]$ lies between $0$ and $1$; numerically $m \approx 0.695$. The other two roots, about $3.06$ and $-3.76$, are outside $[0, 2]$.)
